# Nell Harcourt

## Overview

- **Age:** 11 at the start of the series (turned 11 in March), now a junior in college (around 19 or 20)  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011), [v3 c25 P39](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0039)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c6 P14](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0014)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v3 c40 P0](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0000)</sub>
- **Origin:** Harborough, Nova Scotia  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011), [v3 c4 P32](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0032), [v3 c4 P33](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0033)</sub>
- **Role:** College student; former schoolteacher at Brierley; writer  <sub>[v1 c38 P36](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0036), [v2 c6 P3](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0003), [v3 c15 P11](../source/v03-c15.md#nw-v03-c15-p0011), [v3 c25 P39](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0039), [v3 c36 P3](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0003)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Lucinda  <sub>[v1 c3 P19](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0019), [v1 c3 P21](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0021)</sub>; Seraphine  <sub>[v1 c3 P21](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0021)</sub>; Carrots  <sub>[v1 c15 P34](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0034)</sub>

## Appearance

Nell is a young woman with a small pointed chin, large gray eyes that shine brightly, and a remarkably lovely nose. She has thick waves of crimson/red hair that she formerly wore in a long plait. Her features are expressive, lighting up dramatically when excited or inspired.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P32](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0032), [v1 c15 P33](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0033), [v1 c27 P15](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0015), [v1 c27 P18](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0018), [v2 c1 P58](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0058), [v3 c4 P56](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0056), [v3 c22 P5](../source/v03-c22.md#nw-v03-c22-p0005)_

## Personality

Nell is imaginative, romantic, highly emotional, and inclined to vivid daydreams and dramatizing her life. She possesses a keen sense of humor, deeply values genuine friendship, and displays intense moral pride and honesty, though her impulsive nature often leads her into comical mishaps. She is determined and hardworking, facing challenges with spirited resilience while maintaining a soft, affectionate heart.

_Sources: [v1 c3 P19](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0019), [v1 c5 P9](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0009), [v1 c15 P31](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0031), [v1 c15 P98](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0098), [v1 c19 P74](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0074), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v2 c2 P33](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0033), [v2 c20 P23](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0023), [v3 c2 P3](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0003), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036)_

## History

Born in Harborough, Nova Scotia to high school teacher Edmund Harcourt and his wife Bertha, Nell was orphaned at an early age. She was sent to St. Brendan's Island and adopted by Thirza at Grey Shutters after an adoption agency error. She grew up in Brierley, attending the local school where she formed a lifelong friendship with Isolde Pembroke and shared a tempestuous rivalry and eventual camaraderie with Hugh Carrow, whom she famously struck with a slate after he teased her about her red hair. After winning the Avery Scholarship at Regent's school, Nell deferred college to teach at the Brierley school for two years to assist Thirza. During her tenure, she helped reunite Miss Rosalind Irving with her long-lost love, Stephen Stanhope. Afterwards, Nell enrolled at Wexcombe college. While attending, her story 'Evadne's Atonement' won a baking powder contest prize when submitted by Isolde, and she later published work in The Youth's Friend. Over time, she declined romantic proposals from Barney Pullen, Hugh Carrow, and Cyril, remaining dedicated to her studies, her writing, and her affection for her home at Grey Shutters.

_Sources: [v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011), [v1 c6 P14](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0014), [v1 c15 P38](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0038), [v1 c36 P7](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0007), [v1 c38 P29](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0029), [v2 c6 P3](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0003), [v2 c28 P54](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0054), [v2 c28 P73](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0073), [v3 c3 P0](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0000), [v3 c8 P13](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0013), [v3 c15 P11](../source/v03-c15.md#nw-v03-c15-p0011), [v3 c20 P48](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0048), [v3 c25 P39](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0039), [v3 c36 P3](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0003), [v3 c38 P35](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0035)_

## Background by volume

- Born in Harborough, Nova Scotia to Edmund and Bertha Harcourt  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011)</sub>
- Orphaned in early childhood  <sub>[v3 c8 P18](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0018), [v3 c21 P20](../source/v03-c21.md#nw-v03-c21-p0020)</sub>
- Adopted by Thirza at Grey Shutters on St. Brendan's Island due to a mistake in adoption arrangements  <sub>[v1 c6 P14](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0014), [v1 c7 P21](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0021), [v3 c15 P10](../source/v03-c15.md#nw-v03-c15-p0010)</sub>

## Quotes

> I turned eleven this past March,” Nell stated, giving in to plain reality with a faint sigh. “And Nova Scotia’s Harborough is where I was born. Edmund Harcourt was my father’s name, and he worked as a teacher at the Harborough High School. Bertha Harcourt was my mother’s name. Don’t you think Edmund and Bertha are beautiful names? I feel so happy that my parents possessed pleasant names. Having a father who was named—oh, for instance Jedediah—would be an actual shame, wouldn’t it?  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011)</sub>

> You vile, spiteful youth!” she cried out with deep emotion. “How could you!  <sub>[v1 c15 P37](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0037)</sub>

> Indeed, I recognized that it was somewhat sinful,” confessed Nell. “However, I believed that committing a small sin was a price worth paying to eliminate red hair. I weighed the consequences, Thirza. Furthermore, I intended to compensate for it by being exceptionally well-behaved in different matters.  <sub>[v1 c27 P22](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0022)</sub>

> I do not believe that is the case, Miss Harcourt, ma’am. Visiting is something Miss Rosalind detests. Three relatives are all she ever pays visits to, and according to her, those calls are made strictly out of family duty. Upon her return after the most recent occasion, she declared that she would no longer go on visits due to family duty. ‘Belinda, I’ve returned home enamored with solitude,’ she tells me, ‘and my wish is to never wander away from my own vine and fig tree again. An effort is made so earnestly by my relatives to turn me into an old woman, and it impacts me poorly.’ Precisely in those words, Miss Harcourt, ma’am. ‘It impacts me very poorly.’ Therefore, I doubt that encouraging her to go on a visit would accomplish anything.  <sub>[v2 c27 P48](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0048)</sub>

> No, it doesn’t,” Nell fired back. “Wasn’t Dan O’Connell the one who said that a man being born in a stable didn't turn him into a horse? I’m Island through and through.  <sub>[v3 c4 P35](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0035)</sub>
